sections.title: Form and uses
sections.text: Cannabis sativa is a highly variable annual herb, from roughly 0.2 to 5 m depending on cultivar and growing conditions. Its palmately divided leaves have sharply toothed leaflets. Plants are usually male or female, though monoecious forms occur. The small dry fruit is about 2.5–5 mm; cultivated seeds are eaten or pressed for oil, and stems are used for fibre.

sections.title: Flowering and image
sections.text: The plate shows the toothed leaflets, flowers and fruit, but does not clearly distinguish male and female plants; the drawing is schematic. Hemp seed and fibre uses should not be conflated with cannabinoid content, which varies among cultivars and legal categories.
